stemMd: For positive $a$, which expression is equivalent to $a^{3/2}a^{-1/4}$?
explanationMd: Add the exponents: 3/2−1/4=6/4−1/4=5/4. Positivity ensures the fractional powers are defined in the usual real-number sense.

distractorRationale.b: This multiplies the exponents and mishandles the product rule.
distractorRationale.c: Exponents are added when multiplying like bases, not multiplied.
distractorRationale.a: The second exponent is negative, so it subtracts one quarter.
